Does corruption exist in Japan?
Ken Hower

I have been to Japan several times. On my latest visit, I went with a friend to a restaurant and watched what happened when we asked for a table.

The first person at the door told us that the restaurant was closed, but my friend spoke with him again and explained why we had come. After a short conversation, another waiter led us inside.

While we waited for dinner, my friend pointed out another group of visitors who had just arrived. They received a different response and left before anyone offered them a table.

A conversation at the table turned to local organizations and the way people understood their role in the community. My friend described an earlier emergency and the support that residents received.

I asked whether those organizations also took part in illegal activity. My friend answered that the situation was complicated, and we continued discussing what it meant for everyday life.
